body:
SCIENTIFIC / PROVENANCE HOLD on exact 16c85d4b390c07f9af0f2b08abd091d9af00335b / cand-4SEC14PYRWZQAYRP9X587Q8ZCG.

The candidate conflates field origin with bundle availability. The primary inventory defines Unknown as public primary records not establishing observed versus derived (docs/design/nfrd-primary-source-inventory.md:40-47), and explicitly classifies Story pair and presentation order as Observation (line 216; survey platform/order fields again at line 255). The diagnostic court then says those fields are Observations in the workbook but Unknown to the minimized bundle solely because the workbook is excluded (docs/design/nfrd-baseball-diagnostic-court.md:177-188). Production encodes and enforces that conflation: StoryAssignment and PresentationOrder are IntakeClass.Unknown in productionLineage and requiredClasses (embed-bench/src/main/scala/storymodel4s/bench/nfrd/intake.scala:337-350,580-585).

That erases a known provenance fact. Exclusion means the observed VALUE is unavailable to this bundle; it does not make the FIELD ORIGIN epistemically unknown. A verified receipt that says Unknown can later be misread as uncertainty about acquisition rather than deliberate minimization, exactly where absence must not masquerade as a value.

Required repair: keep both field origins Observation and represent availability/coverage separately, e.g. Excluded or Unavailable with the excluded survey artifact/reason bound into lineage and the receipt. An equally honest narrow alternative is to remove these from the value-bearing ledger and add a separate total expected-field availability ledger, but do not relabel provenance. Add mutation courts for both fields: Observation to Unknown must fail, and Excluded/Unavailable to Available or omission must fail while preserving aggregate-only diagnostics.

UpstreamTechnicalLoss remains correctly Unknown; the existing court at NfrdBaseballSuite.scala:492-539 tests only that distinct case and does not kill this conflation. No other scientific finding is asserted yet.
